task: Read and choose the delivery inspector actions with enlarged text.
audience: People reviewing delivery details, including those using larger text.
scope: Synthetic 420px inspector within a 1440px viewport, 32px text; baseline critique plus verified composition repair.
identityToPreserve: Olive primary action, clear secondary action, larger text and existing spacing.
strengths: Both actions retain meaningful visible labels and contrasting priority; no text is clipped.

scenarios.evidence: Fixture increases CSS text size; browser zoom and assistive technology were not tested.

adaptation.reason: In the baseline, fixed 180px action bases retain two narrow columns at enlarged text, producing tall fragmented labels despite zero audit findings.
adaptation.tradeoff: Stacking actions takes a different scan path; the repair preserves DOM/action order and compares normal and grown text.

findings.location: 420 CSS px inspector, 1440 CSS px viewport, 32px fixture text
findings.observation: Before: each action is 187px wide and 258px tall, with no overflow/clipping finding. Visual inspection shows fragmented multiline labels.
findings.intendedRelationship: Related actions should remain readable as text grows while keeping their priority and order.
findings.consequence: Inferred reading friction from fragmented action wording; no task time or comprehension measurement.
findings.proposal: Use a text-relative 11.25em flex basis in this fixture instead of 180px, allowing actions to stack when enlarged text needs space.
findings.preserve: 32px text, primary/secondary colors, 12px gap, DOM/action order and full labels.
findings.alternative: Keep horizontal actions if actual labels and available space remain readable; the exact basis is a local design hypothesis, not a universal rule.
findings.verification: After: actions are 386px wide and 114px tall, stacked in original order with no clipping. Five captures exercise 300/420px containers, normal/long grown text and an intentionally broken fixed-width variant. Real zoom remains untested.

unknowns: Actual user comprehension and task speed were not measured.
Simulated CSS text growth is not a real zoom or assistive-technology test.
